correctness.rationale: For all h>0 and 0<w<4, symbolic expansion of the actual polynomial source field yields z-dot=-x+w(h-2x^2-z^2)z/(2h) and q-dot=wq(1-q). The Riccati projective ratio z/x lifts to psi-double-dot+(w/2)q psi-dot+psi=0. Direct Gauss substitution gives a pair of complex-conjugate hypergeometric basis functions on each radial component. Their Wronskian has nonzero leading coefficient 2i Omega near q=1 and remains nonzero by Abel uniqueness. Projective lifting reconstructs every trajectory; its coefficient phase changes exactly by -Omega t because c-dot=-wc and its linear lift changes only by a positive real normalization. The on-cycle formula is the continuous limit. The exact cycle vector plus exponentially converging hypergeometric series yields the claimed O(exp(-wt)) asymptotic for each fixed initial point. A symbolic source-field check and multiple mpmath/scipy numerical phase-covariance tests corroborate critical algebra, but the analytical argument supplies the proof.

originality.rationale: Source [1] establishes the polynomial oscillator, its non-autonomous integral, attraction, and invariant oval, but does not provide an exact original-time off-cycle flow or global asymptotic phase. The full text of the closest same-oscillator public finding [2] derives on-cycle density, period and Floquet statistics, not off-cycle phase. A different 2024 degree-six model [3] and a three-dimensional phase-gauge example [4] do not imply the claimed two-dimensional hypergeometric phase. Relevant published-finding corpus and primary literature searches did not locate an equivalent statement. Classical Riccati linearization, hypergeometric Gauss equation and general isochron theory are credited as known tools; unindexed equivalent literature remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed older integrable-oscillator article could include the same projective Gauss solution or its explicit asymptotic phase under another variable name.
The general Riccati-to-hypergeometric method is classical and cannot be claimed novel.
Only the description, not full text, was inspected for the separate three-dimensional phase-gauge result; its explicit model differs and is not a decisive coverage candidate.
Very near w=4 or extreme radii, the complex Gauss evaluation may be poorly conditioned; no uniform error guarantees are asserted.

value.rationale: A full-basin asymptotic phase map is essential for comparing synchronization of trajectories and exact phase assignment under initial-value perturbations. The original qualitative invariant and existing cycle-only physical-time laws do not supply it. The result solves a genuine global timing/geometry problem for a specified nontrivial high-degree polynomial oscillator and gives a physical-time trajectory formula inside and outside the oval. This is more substantive than numerical re-expression of a known period or a routine restatement of the algebraic orbit. Limits: no noisy estimator, no perturbation robustness, no general class result.
